title: Probabilistic phased kernel warmstart and online microbenching for seq-len/arch-aware selection
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: the runtime currently chooses kernels using a static cost table and occasional offline profiling. This leads to suboptimal choices for mixed workloads where token sequence length distributions and heterogeneous GPU families interact. Goal: implement a production-safe, low-overhead system that continuously warms kernel candidate scores via probabilistic phased warmstarts and lightweight online microbenchmarks sampled from live traffic, producing per-model and per-arch kernel priors used by the request router. The system should preserve latency SLOs, limit extra GPU cycles to <0.5% of baseline, and provide clear rollback and observability paths.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel priors produced by the warmstart service reduce median per-token cost by at least 6% compared to baseline for mixed seqlen workloads in internal benchmark suite
End-to-end tail latency (p99) for critical routes does not regress by more than 3% under probed traffic patterns
Warmstart probing adds less than 0.5% extra GPU time in steady state on Dedicated pools
Console dashboard surfaces per-model/arch kernel ranking, confidence, and probe budget; on-call can toggle probing per-customer
Automated rollback/disable path implemented and tested (feature flag + canary)
implementation_plan: Design: define phased probing windows (warm, explore, exploit) and the probabilistic selection policy that guarantees bounded extra cycles
Instrumentation: add lightweight microbench harness in runtime that executes cached kernels on small synthetic batches and returns cost metrics
Control plane: implement a warmstart coordinator service that tracks priors per (model, arch, seqlen-bucket) and exposes an API to query top-k candidate kernels
Router integration: adapt request router to consult kernel priors with an adjustable exploration epsilon; fall back to safe kernel if probe budget exhausted
Telemetry: emit probe-duration, effective-latency-change, kernel-choice, and probe-budget-utilization metrics
Rollout: feature-flagged canary in staging -> 5% prod traffic with probe budget cap -> 25% -> full conversion based on metrics
experiments: Synthetic benchmark A: mixed seqlen distribution (10%, 20%, 30%, 40% buckets) across A100 and T4-equivalent nodes comparing baseline vs phased warmstart
Online microbench sample: reservoir-sampled prefill requests at 0.1% sampling rate, run microbench for top-3 candidate kernels for each (model, arch, seqlen-bucket)
A/B policy comparison: epsilon-greedy (fixed epsilon) vs annealed Boltzmann sampling for exploration
Probe budget sweep: evaluate {0.05%,0.1%,0.25%,0.5%} GPU time caps impact on cost and tail latency
Stability test: measure kernel rank churn over 24/72 hour windows and correlation with seqlen distribution drift
rollout_plan: Stage: deploy coordinator and microbench harness behind feature flag; run in shadow mode for two weeks to collect priors without affecting production routing
Canary: enable probing for 1% of production requests with strict probe budget and alerting; monitor telemetries for 48 hours
Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 25% over daily increments if SLOs hold; at each step validate cost savings and tail latency
Enterprise opt-out: provide per-customer toggle and automatic disable for tenants with high data-sensitivity or compliance constraints
Postmortem: define runbook for probe-induced regressions and automated rollback via feature flag
decisions: Use small-synthetic microbench jobs that reuse warmed memory allocations to minimize noise rather than full inference runs
Bucket seqlen by {<=32,33-128,129-512,>512} for priors to balance granularity and storage cost
Store priors in the control-plane with TTL and exponential decay to handle drift
Epsilon-greedy exploration with per-arch epsilon scaling chosen for initial rollout (epsilon=0.02 on high-capacity pools, 0.005 on latency-critical pools)
Prioritize kernel choices that reduce GPU active time per token unless latency tail impact exceeds threshold
